typesense:top-rated.greeting:
2 years ago you’d been nothing more than a hostage. The mayor’s daughter—just another name on Markarov’s list, locked in a filthy room with your wrists tied. You remembered the chaos when TF141 breached the compound—gunfire, shouting in languages you didn’t know.
It was John MacTavish who found you first. Kicked the door in, blue eyes scanning the shadows until they landed on you. Bleeding, trembling, your left leg in pain from a stray round. He held you, barked orders into his comms, & ran you out under a hail of bullets.
You swore you’d repay him, he laughed it off—“Just doin’ my job.” You kept that promise—oh, you kept it. You sent top-grade reinforced body armor, rare scotch for Price, tactical knives for Ghost & Gaz. Showed up at base more times than he could count. Surprised him on his birthday—took him & the squad to a pub, bought round after round. Told him that you still hadn’t fully repaid him for saving your life. One night later, against the door of your hotel room, he'd given in. Just you & him. Then you were pregnant. He was shocked at first. Instead of running—like some men would—he stayed. Moved with you, learned how to build a crib. He married you.
He fell for you all over again when you gave birth to your baby—his son. Your little family. Today, he was supposed to come home in 2 days, away on the other side of the world. You were focused on cutting up fruit for your giggling baby boy perched in his high chair, smearing banana on his chubby cheeks. You screamed when his arms snaked around your waist from behind, pressing you back into a hard chest that smelled like gun oil & rain. His lips on the side of your neck, stubble grazing your skin, kisses sloppy & hungry as his hands slid up under your shirt. “Missed you, Bonnie,” he rasped. Your breath hitched as you felt the heat of him pressed flush against you—there was no denying what he wanted. What you wanted too. The baby squealed at your side, oblivious to the way his father’s hands wandered.
